name: Protactinium
occurrence: Extremely rare and found only in trace amounts within uranium ores as a decay product; one of the scarcest naturally occurring elements.
majorUses: No significant practical applications — studied almost exclusively for nuclear physics and geological dating research
safetyNotes: Highly radioactive and toxic; one of the rarest and most expensive elements on Earth to obtain even in research quantities.
notableCharacteristics: Its name means 'parent of actinium', since it decays into actinium — one of the few elements literally named for what it turns into rather than what it currently is.
whyHere: Sitting between thorium and uranium, protactinium's electrons begin genuinely filling the 5f subshell, marking a true transition point where actinide chemistry starts to diverge from the earlier, more lanthanide-like actinium and thorium.
didYouKnow: Protactinium is so rare and difficult to extract that the world's entire known supply, painstakingly recovered from processing tonnes of uranium ore residue, amounts to only a few hundred grams.
genZNote: Named after what it eventually decays into rather than what it currently is. Living life named after its own future.
